steps.content: In the distance, a luxury car brazenly drives against traffic in broad daylight, executing one final stylish drift before coming to a stop at the hotel entrance.
[Luxury Hotel]
This enigmatic woman flouts DisCity's rules without hesitation, carving her own path in all things, yet surprisingly, she's chosen to meet at a very public place.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I hear this is where they host the famous "Parfait's Dinner Party," so the food has to be good. Order whatever you want. My treat.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: But that companion of yours hiding at the table behind us can pay for himself, since he wouldn't even do us the honor of joining us.

Of course he won't join you—that's an agent of the 9th Agency here to secretly ensure your safety. The woman before you seems to know this all too well, and might have even noticed Schorl hidden in your coat pocket.
After all, she has deliberately instructed the server to take your coat away, claiming it was for some "dinner etiquette."

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Name's Catherine. I'm usually on the road for my business, so DisCity visits are rare for me. I'd like to actually stay and look around this time.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: How's that gift I gave you? I mean, that girl who dances with the blades.
For a moment, you pause and study her expression. Her eyes hold no ill intent, just an offhanded interest.

The listening device on you is still active. 9th hasn't sent over her identity details yet, but there's been no warning from his side either. You're clear to keep talking—this will also help the agents gather intel.
Since she was the original "buyer," you figure Catherine must be curious about Jasmine's situation. You describe her current condition briefly, without going into much detail.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I see... a perfect "victim." She's the reason why you're upset? Hmm... looks like the young generation has barely seen war these days.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...Heh, you're surprisingly bad at hiding your emotions. She's the reason why you're upset?
You ramble on while she just watches you in silence. Finally, she gives a soft laugh, as if she sees right through you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why did you buy her, only to give her to me?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I was only interested in her blades. Since you seemed to care about her as a person, I just went along with what worked for everyone.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Are those blades at the FAC now? I'll go pick them up later.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Let's talk more about that girl. She's the reason why you're upset? Looks like the young generation has barely seen war these days.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: You can talk to me about it. I've seen war myself.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: My family's been in arms for generations. We used to have connections with the former DisCity military and made our fortune through it—war has always been good business. When I caught wind of tension at the Great Expo, I came to see where the opportunities lie. Same as always.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If tensions between DisCity and Fraser escalate, I could make another fortune and treat you to dinner a few times.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Just giving an example—nothing special, just how things usually go.
She places cash on the table and rises to her feet.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I can see you've lost your appetite. The food here is mediocre anyway. Let's go somewhere else.
You glance back at your agent companion, who signals for you to follow her.
She guides you out of the hotel and toward the sleek luxury sports car parked by the curb. All eyes turn to her, seemingly captivated by her commanding presence.
You slide into the car as planned and instinctively glance at the rearview mirror. The 9th Agency's agent should be tailing you to keep you safe.

Before you can react, the woman slams her foot on the accelerator, and the car lurches forward with a surge of speed. In the rearview mirror, 9th's disguised vehicle shrinks into the distance—utterly immobilized, powerless to give chase.

steps.speaker: Option
options: What in the world are you up to?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Just shaking off a few tails so we can have some privacy. It's not like I'm kidnapping you or anything—relax.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: We're on a main road with people all around. What's there to be afraid of? Just don't make a scene or I'll end up with a ticket.
She's been driving against traffic in broad daylight and making illegal stops. Since when does she care about DisCity's rules or traffic tickets?
You check your communication terminal—no messages from the agent. Meanwhile, Schorl lies silent in your pocket, completely unresponsive.

It seems she's not just an arms dealer, and her ties to DisCity go deeper than you expected. In fact, she might be a high-ranking official working undercover. You wonder if this is some new kind of evaluation test.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: The fight hasn't even started, and you're already choking for air. Lighten up, you can't run from what's coming anyway.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: As long as this city-state remains built on Hypercubes, war is unavoidable. Doesn't matter who fires the first shot or what flag they wave. This place will always be ground zero. You can hate war all you want, but that won't stop it. Time to wake up.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Know your place, adapt to survive, then do whatever it takes to achieve your goals—whether they're for war or peace.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: This conversation can wait. For now, just focus on enjoying the moment while you can.

She glides through DisCity's streets with practiced ease, the car slicing through the night unhindered. Neon reflections streak across her glasses, while the windshield paints itself in the city's ever-shifting hues. For a moment, the world outside blurs into a dream, the vehicle adrift in a river of hues.

Catherine steers with one hand, the other stretched out the window—fingers splayed as if to catch the rushing wind and the streaking lights. A faint smile plays at the corner of her lips, etched by the flickering shadows. Only then do you realize the speedometer has surged past 300.
Without warning, a colossal shadow surges across your path. Tires shriek against the road as the car lurches violently, nearly causing you to lose your dinner.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: DisCity's peace has its charms...

She's been driving at breakneck speed, and though it feels like barely any time has passed, you suddenly find yourself at the MBCC. That violent drift just now was because you nearly crashed into the Bureau's exterior wall.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Yeah.
Your voice trembles uncontrollably as she opens the door, disengages all the security locks, and lets you out of the car.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Time to get out, sir. Get some rest.
steps.female_content: Time to get out, miss. Get some rest.

steps.content: That's... it? No kidnapping, no coercion, no elaborate schemes—not even some kind of evaluation like you suspected.
After days of unrelenting tension, these fleeting hours of unexpected calm feel surreal, almost deceptive. You stare at her, utterly bewildered.

steps.speaker: Option
options: ...So what do you really want from me?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Didn't I already tell you?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: You looked like you needed air. So I drove. Good night.

You've barely taken two steps when your comm device buzzes with a flurry of notifications. The signal is back—your agent companion wasn't silent after all. The messages had been blocked by the person behind you.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Hahaha!

You watch her drive away, biting back the dozen retorts burning on your tongue. At least the dinner was decent. And she did give you a ride home. Pulling your coat tighter against the chill, you turn and start walking back.
When you instinctively slide your hand into your pocket, your fingers touch something unexpected. You're certain it wasn't there when you left the Bureau today.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: This is... an invitation?
You quickly grasp the meaning behind this gesture, tuck away the envelop, and hurry back to the Bureau.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Get me the 9th Agency on the line, and everyone at the City-State Security Bureau. Also schedule an internal meeting here at the Bureau. And...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Is Elvira here? I need to speak with her.
At least she did make a fair point.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Know your place, adapt to survive, then do whatever it takes to achieve your goals—whether they're for war or peace.
[Scene Change] Hospital
Max King walks down this hallway once again, but he never expected to find two people—who shouldn't be here—standing outside the room.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: What are you doing here?! Tell me no one followed you. Are you out of your mind?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Nightmare is keeping watch. If anyone comes, it will alert us.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: If you, the Speaker, can slip in here alone without drawing attention, then I won't be noticed either.

He should have laughed it off, deflected with a joke, sent them on their way—but he doesn't have the energy anymore. His tie strangles him, a noose disguised as silk. Max King tugs at it, even the motion draining what little strength he has left.
With a sigh, he ignores the two kids and walks on by himself.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: That Chief sent you here, didn't he? Stop with all this sneaking around. It'll cause trouble if someone catches you. Tell him to make a proper appointment.
steps.female_content: That Chief sent you here, didn't she? Stop with all this sneaking around. It'll cause trouble if someone catches you. Tell her to make a proper appointment.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: But best to lay low for now. If you're trying to help the West District, don't draw attention. Too many eyes are watching.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ${PlayerName}'s friend in the West District says you're the one who needs help. You're trying your best to deal with them carefully, but you don't know who you can trust.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Haha, you've got it all wrong. I'm just trying to keep my seat secure. My position is very fragile, so I have no choice but to fight with everything I've got.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Or... is the West District actually trying to win me over now? They want a puppet Speaker?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: What's in it for you?

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...I don't know. But ${PlayerName} said if we found you here, we could talk to you.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: He said you can be trusted when you're here.
steps.female_content: She said you can be trusted when you're here.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: What exactly is he trying to get at?
steps.female_content: What exactly is she trying to get at?

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I know some names. What they want, the cards they're holding, and the leverage against them. I can show you the cracks in the high-ups—the ones you're not seeing.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I remember every word Stewart told me. And now I'm giving you his true legacy. This is your weapon now.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ${PlayerName} wants me to tell you this: Do whatever you think is right, Mr. Speaker Max King. He trusts you.
steps.female_content: ${PlayerName} wants me to tell you this: Do whatever you think is right, Mr. Speaker Max King. She trusts you.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Trust... me?
[Scene Change]
After making all the arrangements, you send Schorl away and head alone to the Banyan special ward to visit Jasmine.
[Scene Change] A softly warm-tinted ring Bureau backdrop as Jasmine's special ward
When you enter, you find her not lying in bed. She's dragged the mattress to the floor by the simulated window, where she's curled up beneath the artificial sunlight, basking in its glow.
You approach her with soft footsteps, reaching out to comfort her with your shackles. She opens her eyes, tilts her head as she sees you, and offers a drowsy smile.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Hehe, what took you so long? I've been waiting for ages.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Work's been crazy lately. We're constantly refining the treatment plan, and it feels like we're so close to a breakthrough. I didn't want to take any breaks.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How are you feeling?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Me? Oh, I feel wonderful. The voices in my head are gone, my scars don't hurt anymore... and now I even have good dreams. Is it because you've been watching over me at night?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The corruptive weapon that was making you uncomfortable has been taken away. It won't affect you anymore.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Oh, that's not it. I just know I'll get better as long as you're by my side. Sibilla was right—you're so strong and kind, always watching over us... and yet you never say a word about it.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: But you always sneak away before I wake up, not giving me a chance to thank you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Well, I need to turn in early. The Great Expo is not over yet, so I have to be there early to ensure everyone's safety.
She giggles, as if seeing through your clumsy lie but choosing not to call you out on it.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: The Great Expo, huh... Well, that doesn't matter because you still came to see me today. It makes me so happy.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: So, are you going to question me now? About Fraser? I don't know much, though. Everything was so confusing. They only fed me empty promises about putting me on stage to perform, but never mentioned what they were really up to.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: And those Outland extremists they mentioned? I have no idea who they are either. I came near DisCity a long time ago, but even though I was right there, I just couldn't find my way in. I ended up tagging along with some desert bandits. They promised they'd take me in if I played bodyguard, but they never actually did...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Oh! Don't tell me you're all right about me being an idiot after all!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're not an idiot, Jasmine. You're just overly sensitive to Mania.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Think of how migrating birds lose their way in magnetic storms. The Mania field in WhiteSands is the same unpredictable, and it hits you hard.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But anyway, you've made it here.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Hehe, I've been pretty lucky. The desert bandits kept me fed, and the Fraser people at least kept their promise of taking me to the Great Expo. And I met someone who was really kind. She told me you are better than anyone else in the world and would definitely make my wish come true.
She leans in closer and speaks in a hushed voice.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I still have one more wish... Chief, could you take me to the closing ceremony? It's tomorrow.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: In my dreams, there's always this celebration that never finishes. I really want to see it through. The Great Expo would be perfect for that. Would you take me there? This is my only wish now. You'll help me, right? I'll repay you, I promise!

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You can ask me anything. I'll do anything for you! Would you like to see me dance? My friend says I'm a great dancer, and the Fraser people say I can mesmerize anyone. I'll dance for you! Just... please take me to the closing ceremony!
Noticing your momentary hesitation, her smile wavers, replaced by a pitiful expression with watery eyes.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Is that not possible? Don't tell me you're going to lock me up and make me fight for you like those desert bandits...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I won't force you into anything, and I understand how you feel. Now, get ready for that celebration you want to finish.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Really? You promise?
She tries to throw her arms around you in excitement, but you gently hold her back.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But in return, I need you to promise me one thing.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Yeah, go ahead.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After the closing ceremony is over, I want you to stay with me. Let's go do something fun together.
She freezes for a moment, confused.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...What do you mean?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've always wanted to visit DisCity, right? Now that you've made it here, you can explore all around. There's so much you can do here—amazing food, fun spots, and beautiful sights. Trust me, it'll be nothing like the places you've been before.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Look how far you've come... Now you can finally try all those things you've been looking forward to. Just say the word, and I'll be right there with you.
She avoids meeting your gaze.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I... never thought about that.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I only know celebrations, nothing else. I never thought about other things, never really cared... I never thought about what would happen after the celebration.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Well... how about we ask some friends for ideas? Once the closing ceremony is over, I won't have to work overtime anymore. I'll have plenty of time. Oh, right!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't you have a good friend? "Sibilla," right? We could go find her together. I'd really like to meet your friend.
She answers with silence, just as you expected.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Let's go find your hometown together.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Don't bother with all that. I forgot about it long ago...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's alright. There has to be someone who remembers.
You pull out the information that you recently asked the 9th Agency to collect. Though the data is sparse, you notice a shift in Jasmine's expression.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I still remember that dream we shared. Your hometown was so alive back then—a bustling little village where everyone celebrated the harvest. They'd light bonfires, and the girls would make flower-woven targets. I remember parade floats rolling through the fields, carrying scarecrows, and fireworks too.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your name, "Jasmine"... I'm sure it was given to you with many lovely blessings. If you can remember its meaning, that would make it easier to trace your origins.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And your dance... it's so beautiful, unlike anything I've ever seen. I'm sure if we ask around, we'll find someone who remembers it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even if your hometown is gone—even if the world has forgotten it—it still lives inside you, in every part of your life. And now, through you, it's become a part of me, too. Let's find it back together.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The war is over. Now we can look forward to the next celebration—bigger and brighter—no matter how long it takes... As long as we live, there will always be another chance.
She listens to you in silence, only whispering a response after a long while.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...You're so kind to me...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Why are you being so kind to me?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You're clearly different from Sibilla, clearly from DisCity...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...But why are you nothing like all the others?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...In your eyes, what should the people of DisCity be like?

Like those who drove her away? The desert bandits who exploited her? The spectators who treated her as nothing more than a spectacle for their amusement? Or... the ruthless soldiers from her dreams who devastated everything?
Jasmine doesn't answer. Her eyelids droop—a fleeting shadow of melancholy, though for all the world she might just be a sun-warmed kitten succumbing to the drowsy contentment.
With a languid stretch, she squints her eyes and curls onto your lap, murmuring something soft and sleep-laden.
Lying across your lap, her brief melancholy fades as quickly as it came. She murmurs lazily in the golden light.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: In DisCity, the only meat I ever ate was sandworms, and they tasted awful... I want to try the amazing food you mentioned.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: And... if DisCity has celebrations or fireworks, I'd like to see them too. Rain, snow... summer, autumn, winter... And if there are more good people around you, I'd like to meet them too.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I like this kind of promise... You have my word, Chief. Take me to the celebration, and I'll come back to you after it's over. Just as promised.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Once the closing ceremony ends... I'll follow you anywhere.
A warm, contented smile brightens her face.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Thank you.
You walk out of the room.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, tomorrow is the closing ceremony. Jasmine...

steps.speaker: Option
options: Take Jasmine to the closing ceremony
Don't take Jasmine to the closing ceremony

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Make sure to completely isolate her from the contamination source—those weapons. I'll do everything possible to control the risk. The shackles should stabilize her, and if she steps out of line, I can hold her down. Besides...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's a promise.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I can't rule out suspicions about her, and I must keep the risk to a minimum. Leave her here, and make sure to take good care of her.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...After everything is over, we can take her to a real celebration.
You gaze at her, confined within the room. Yet, in return, she offers you an innocent, joyful smile.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: See you then!
[Scene Change]
Several security personnel meticulously examine the tightly sealed hazardous item—a "performance prop" confiscated from the Outlander dancer detained by MBCC.
The higher-ups require inspections every three hours with several specific metrics to check, but they haven't explained the reasoning behind this requirement.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: They've surely got it locked down tight. After all these years, how did a weapon from ████ end up with some Outlander? No wonder FAC is so worked up. Once they classify this information, the thing will probably never see the light of day.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.content: What a waste for such a weapon to just gather dust...
He sets down the items and closes the door. Behind multiple layers of security, the crimson blades flash with a deadly gleam.
